\[
P(f) = M \frac{F(f)}{|F(f)|},\quad g = \operatorname{Re} \mathcal{F}^{-1}\{P\}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(F\): The spectrum of the extended image
- \(M\): The mean magnitude of F
- \(P\): The spectrum with every magnitude set to M

F is the spectrum of the image extended with the border mode, and M its mean magnitude. Every frequency keeps its phase and gets the magnitude M. Oppenheim and Lim showed that the phase holds most of what makes an image recognizable, so the result still shows the edges and lines. Using M keeps the scale of the image. Magnitudes below 1e-9 times the largest count as 0, so frequencies that a mirror extension makes 0 stay 0 instead of turning rounding noise into content.
